cands.name: Jared Sluss

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama State Senate District 7 in 2026, facing incumbent Republican Sam Givhan. He has a UAB public health degree and says he spent nine years in affordable housing, neighborhood development and small business ownership. No elected office is on record.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (a Sway voting group) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (a Sway voting group).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jared Sluss was born or raised, or when he moved to Alabama. We found no record of elected office or of any bills he sponsored. His stated work history comes only from his own campaign site, and we could not check employers or dates. We found no statements from him on homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun rights, or abortion. We found no documented position on building new data centers beyond his criticism of their tax breaks. No news coverage or controversies were found.

qual.background: He says he has a UAB public health degree and nine years of work in affordable housing, neighborhood development and small business ownership. No legislative or other elected service is documented.
qual.why: Small business ownership and housing and neighborhood development work fall in the middle band. No prior legislative service or policy-staff or budget career was found, and the work history is self-reported on his campaign site.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Said on his campaign site that 16 years of one-party rule in Alabama has meant 'billions in tax breaks to data centers' alongside unreliable healthcare and unaffordable living. This criticizes data-center tax breaks; he did not state a ban or moratorium.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Pledged to pay teachers and support staff, and to fully fund pre-K and school meals. He said nothing about vouchers, charters or school choice on the pages read.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Sam Givhan

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama District 7 since 2018. Real estate attorney with a finance degree from Auburn and a law degree from the University of Alabama. Former chairman of the Madison County Republican Party (2014–2018). His campaign site lists him as a land and development company owner.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Sam Givhan was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama; his campaign site calls him a seventh-generation Alabama farmer but gives no place or dates. We found no specific statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site speaks only in general terms about attracting investment, lower taxes and public safety. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The pages we had list no sponsored bills, so we could not cite any specific legislation he wrote. Ballotpedia identified no endorsements for him in 2026. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: Alabama state senator since November 2018, with Judiciary vice-chair and Finance and Tax committee seats. Real estate attorney (Lanier Ford, per his campaign site), owner of Houston Land Company and SHG Development, and Madison County Republican Party chairman 2014–2018.
qual.why: Nearly eight years of legislative service, including budget-related committee work, plus a law career and business ownership. Committee seats were not counted toward the score.
